written: 2026-11-01, before match 132877 was tracked or any of its results computed
question: Does the candidate ball track (default since PR #318) stay at least as good as the production ball on a daylight match the system has never seen?
match: SoccerTrack v2 132877 (Test Videos set; never used for training, tuning or any decision), first half panorama, daylight, University of Tsukuba pitch
window: match minutes 10-20 of the first half: video seconds padding+600 ... padding+1200, padding = 2007 s from 132877_padding_info.csv (FIRST_HALF); 20 segments of 30 s. If the video does not cover this range, the window is the first 20 full segments after kickoff and this is noted before evaluation
pipeline: same as 117092 control: track_live_candidates, v2 weights, tiles 4, track-fps 15, frames at 12.5 fps, camera static, landmark TPS calibration from 132877_keypoints.json (calibration_from_keypoints); home attack direction from the event mapping
event_mapping: derive_event_mapping on tracked players only (no ball, no possession) for axis flips and team side; video offset fixed in advance = padding - 0.28 s (the GSR-measured lag on 117092); the player-derived best offset is reported but not used

arms.candidate: refine_segment with defaults at the commit of this file

criteria.D1: touch hit within 5 m: candidate >= baseline - 2 points
criteria.D2: touch wrong-ball share: candidate <= baseline + 2 points
criteria.D3: pass-flight hit within 5 m: candidate >= baseline - 5 points
criteria.D4: defending-team accuracy on drawn frames (eval_defending_events): candidate >= baseline - 2 points
criteria.D5: correct defending share of all possession frames: candidate >= baseline - 2 points

decision: all pass -> the candidate track stays the default with daylight evidence added to the scorecard. Any failure -> reported as a daylight limit, backlog item opened; code and criteria are not changed after seeing the result
not_measured_here: end-to-end block-label accuracy (needs GSR player table, not downloaded for this match)
